rule: GOAL: Fill four slots with specific colors to match a target sequence at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a bottom button to select a color, indicated by a white border. Click a target slot to place the selected color. RULE: Each color can be used only once; the button turns gray after placement. TRAP: Thinking slots are filled by clicking buttons directly, rather than selecting a button first.

GOAL: Guide the player to the green exit using the shortest path across the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two cells in the chosen direction. RULE: Moves are only valid if the intermediate and destination cells are not black walls. TRAP: Believing movement slides until a wall stops you, rather than moving a fixed distance.

GOAL: Guide the purple square to the blue circle by clicking forward dots. CONTROLS: Click green dots two steps ahead to move the square diagonally. RULE: Each click advances the square exactly two cells toward the target. TRAP: Clicking dots not precisely two steps ahead wastes moves or fails entirely.

GOAL: Push the gray piston right to align with the yellow gap in the wall. CONTROLS: Click the blue block to slide the piston horizontally. RULE: Gray fills all space left of the piston, creating a solid barrier. TRAP: Believing clicking the yellow gap or gray area moves things; only the blue block responds.

GOAL: Move each colored plug's tip to its matching plus marker. CONTROLS: Clicking a panel shifts that plug three spaces along its track. RULE: Only the final position matters; overshooting or stopping short fails the check. TRAP: Assuming the center dot must align with the plus; actually, the tip must touch it.

GOAL: Guide the falling stream into the notch. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the platform; space locks it. RULE: Align the platform edge to direct the liquid flow. TRAP: Covering the stream fully makes it spread both ways instead of one.

GOAL: Align the yellow piston with the green gap in the lower wall. CONTROLS: Click the middle band to expand it from the top; click the bottom band to push the piston right. RULE: The piston only moves if the middle band has enough white space to shrink into. TRAP: Believing you could push the piston without first refilling the middle band from the top, causing wasted clicks.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket by moving it strictly downward five times to close the circuit. CONTROLS: Clicking bar or stem segments toggles their color between white and black to set the path. Clicking the circle button executes the movement sequence. RULE: The plug only moves down when both the bar and stem at each position are black, requiring all ten segments to be black for five steps. TRAP: Assuming partial black segments allow movement or that the plug can move horizontally; it requires a fully black vertical path for straight descent.

GOAL: Arrange colors in the correct sequence to clear the level. CONTROLS: Swap adjacent tiles to reorder them; press Space to verify the current arrangement. RULE: Read the sequence starting with red slots, continuing through the green box, and ending with the final red slot. TRAP: Assuming the decorative ring counts as a distinct position in the reading order wastes time.

GOAL: Arrange five glyphs into a specific cyclic sequence to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate individual glyph slots forward or backward through their unique order. RULE: Each color follows a strict, repeating cycle; rotation is the only way to align items. TRAP: Assuming all slots share the same starting position; they do not, requiring independent tracking.

GOAL: Place colored tokens into slots to satisfy ring constraints. CONTROLS: Click palette button, then click target slot. RULE: Read sub-boxes left-to-right, continuing sequentially through all rings. TRAP: Assuming palette buttons stay in fixed positions; they shift after use.

GOAL: Match the keypad pattern to a plus shape to shrink the block to fit the socket. CONTROLS: Arrows moved or rotated the block; clicking lit specific keypad cells. RULE: Solving the pattern changed the block’s dimensions, requiring precise alignment for insertion. TRAP: Assuming random clicks worked; only the exact plus shape triggered the size change.

GOAL: Move the block up the vertical track into the top socket. CONTROLS: Click keypad cells to match the pattern; press arrows to move the block. RULE: The block shrinks to 2x2 only after the keypad pattern is correctly lit. TRAP: Believing the block could pass the narrow neck while still 4x4.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the patrolling guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step; the guard lunges toward you. RULE: The guard attacks if you stand in its row within two tiles. TRAP: Thinking you can stand adjacent to the guard safely; proximity triggers a fatal lunge.

GOAL: Align pistons to clear walls using water transfer. CONTROLS: Click columns to pump water between adjacent bands. RULE: Donors must stay above limits; receivers must not overflow. TRAP: Assuming empty bands can donate; they cannot, wasting clicks.

GOAL: Insert the green sequence into the red box to match the target order. CONTROLS: Click the ring tool to place a marker, then click slots to swap pieces. RULE: The ring acts as an insertion point; the green box’s contents fill the sequence starting at the ring’s location. TRAP: Thinking the ring was a permanent border piece; it is a movable token that defines where insertion happens.

GOAL: Align seven shape wheels to match a specific sequence of classes. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the selection cursor; pressing the button cycles the current wheel forward. RULE: Matching ignores rotation, so any orientation of the correct shape class counts as a match. TRAP: Assuming exact pose alignment is required wastes time trying to force specific rotations instead of just cycling to the right shape.

GOAL: Arrange a five-slot sequence to match a target string containing two identical repeating blocks. CONTROLS: Click source tokens or ring buttons, then click destination slots to place items; press space to submit. RULE: The two ring buttons each generate the same three-item block, so place them in adjacent target positions. TRAP: Assuming rings create unique patterns wastes time; they always produce identical sequences, so pair them immediately.

ESTABLISHED: Walls are absent. Moves are jumps, not sweeps. Blocked moves rotate in place. FAILED: No specific failed attempts listed, but budget is exceeded. GOAL IS NOT: Not yet determined. CONTROLS: Movement jumps. Blocked moves rotate. Space attaches or drops.

GOAL: Arrange three nested boxes to form a specific color sequence. CONTROLS: Click rings to set box order, then click palette colors to fill empty slots. RULE: The first color of each box determines its position in the final sequence. TRAP: Assuming boxes stay fixed; you must reorder them by placing rings into the parent container.

GOAL: Move three boxes into the target row using a sliding player. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the player; Space attaches or drops a box. RULE: The player must slide past a box to push it, not bump it directly. TRAP: Thinking the player pushes boxes like ice blocks; here, you must maneuver around them to attach and relocate.

GOAL: Fit the block into the blue socket by passing through the restricted gate. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; clicking the keypad zaps it to shrink size. RULE: The block only shrinks to two units when zapped next to the keyway teeth. TRAP: Assuming the gate blocks movement; it actually allows passage if the block is small.

GOAL: Match the seven-color sequence by nesting shapes. CONTROLS: Click to place rings inside boxes and colors in slots. RULE: Rings expand into three slots, shifting the total sequence length. TRAP: Treating boxes as separate items instead of nested containers.

GOAL: Rotate seven dials to match target symbols. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor; up/down rotate dial. RULE: Dials cycle through six distinct states in a fixed order. TRAP: Assuming random rotation; knowing the sequence allows shortest path calculation.

GOAL: Reach the exit after clearing three guards. CONTROLS: Arrows move one space along corridors. RULE: Guards are destroyed only when entering their tile. TRAP: Believing guards block movement; they do not, so moving through them clears the path.

GOAL: You needed to chain color transformations, mapping starting shapes through an intermediate set to find the correct final yellow symbols for each slot. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the cursor between slots and rotated the symbol wheels to change their displayed value. RULE: Each starting shape uniquely identified an intermediate symbol, which in turn pointed to the specific target yellow symbol. TRAP: Assuming all visible symbols were valid targets; some were decoys not connected to any valid transformation chain.

GOAL: Guide the yellow plus to align its arms with hidden dots inside charcoal boxes. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the plus; space toggles selection between pieces. RULE: The plus’s center must sit exactly on the intersection of the target dots’ row and column. TRAP: Assuming the plus must touch each dot individually; it only needs to cross the correct lines.

GOAL: Rotate the ring of blocks to align the marker with the correct corner. CONTROLS: Clicking a specific block on the perimeter rotates the entire loop. RULE: Only the block nearest the yellow marker responds to input; others are inert. TRAP: Clicking random blocks or the plus symbols wastes moves, as only the active cursor block triggers the rotation.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a highlighted target to jump over an adjacent piece. RULE: Jumps must land on empty spaces directly beyond an adjacent piece, capturing the jumped piece. TRAP: Assuming any piece can move; only pieces with valid adjacent partners and landing spots are playable.

GOAL: Match the large grid to its small reference pattern by changing colors. CONTROLS: Click a square to flip its color. RULE: The small icon shows exactly which squares must be red. TRAP: Assuming a complex puzzle where clicking affects neighbors; it only changes the clicked square.

GOAL: Match the bottom legend glyph to the top box glyph by moving a block onto a plus sign. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; six actions were needed to reach the target. RULE: Covering the plus shifts the legend's active unit, aligning it with the static box pattern. TRAP: Believing a match meant instant completion; the block must stay on the plus to finish.

GOAL: Position the octagon inside the target ring by aligning two diamond anchors. CONTROLS: Clicking a diamond moves it to that spot; clicking a different diamond swaps their positions. RULE: The octagon always sits exactly at the midpoint between the two diamond anchors. TRAP: Thinking clicks only move the active piece; clicking the stationary gray diamond actually swaps their colors.

GOAL: Set specific grid blocks to orange to match hidden patterns. CONTROLS: Clicking a block toggles its color between blue and orange. RULE: Each motif reveals the target colors of its surrounding eight blocks, with overlapping hints confirming the solution. TRAP: Assuming the motif’s center cell itself needed changing; it is merely a reference point, not a clickable target.

GOAL: Move the two yellow blocks onto the dashed squares. CONTROLS: Clicking a button shifts blocks along its specific track; A moves forward, B and C move backward. RULE: Blocks wrap around their track, so moving forward from the end lands you at the start. TRAP: Assuming clicks move blocks in the direction of the arrow; actually, they move opposite to the visual indicator.

GOAL: Align the blue plus symbol to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Space places or rotates the piece. RULE: Shapes snap to grid intersections, requiring precise alignment of all arms. TRAP: Assuming diagonal moves were allowed; you must navigate orthogonally around obstacles.

GOAL: Slide two blocks from opposite sides to swap their starting positions by passing through the top corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected block one space in that direction; blocks cannot pass through each other or walls. RULE: Blocks occupy single cells, so they must approach the top bar from opposite ends to cross without collision. TRAP: Trying to force a block past another in the narrow side corridors wastes moves; you must go up and around.

GOAL: Paint the grid using overlapping hints to reveal the hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors and inspect motif centers. RULE: White marks the center color; gray marks the opposite color. TRAP: Assuming gray always means red ignores that it flips based on the hint’s center.

ESTABLISHED: Three blocks can dock in the left column, but the level remains unsolved. The ring moves vertically and extends horizontally to hook or push blocks. FAILED: Docking all three blocks while the ring is at row 24 did not trigger a win. Re-hooking blocks during retraction causes unwanted movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing all three blocks in the left column regardless of the ring's final position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the ring. Extending the ring horizontally hooks blocks for dragging or pushes them if obstructed.

GOAL: Transform the grid to match a hidden pattern using limited moves. CONTROLS: Clicking cycles colors from blue to red to orange. RULE: Only specific cells need changing; others must remain blue. TRAP: Over-clicking ambiguous cells wastes moves when leaving them blue was sufficient.

GOAL: Move the yellow block to its target zone and the orange block to its own. CONTROLS: Left and Right buttons rotate their respective rings clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Rings share two central cells, allowing blocks to transfer between the left and right sides. TRAP: Assuming rings are independent; failing to use shared cells for transfer leads to dead ends.

GOAL: Place both rings into their matching sockets to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active ring; clicking a dot swaps which ring is active. RULE: Pushing a ring into a wall portal instantly transports it to the corresponding panel on the other side. TRAP: Assuming a ring stays inert after moving; you must click its dot to activate it before positioning.

GOAL: Move three shapes into their target outlines. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the selected shape. Space locks it in place. RULE: Shapes fit perfectly when pixels align. TRAP: Assuming the cursor stays on the active shape. It moves with the block, causing you to select the wrong piece next.

GOAL: Place shapes to form valid rings using chain endpoints and centroids. CONTROLS: Click gray diamonds to flip their state and click empty cells to place new shapes. RULE: Rings require specific centroid coordinates calculated by averaging the positions of their three component shapes. TRAP: Assuming all shapes must be flipped first; some chains require placing new shapes to satisfy centroid math.

GOAL: Turn all visible blocks green to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click a block to flip it and its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Plus symbols indicate special blocks that still toggle neighbors normally. TRAP: Believing plus blocks behaved differently, causing unnecessary double-clicks to correct.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange pieces to the bottom-right cross. CONTROLS: Up and down arrows spin the vertical column; left and right arrows spin the horizontal row. RULE: The vertical and horizontal cycles intersect at four specific points, allowing pieces to switch tracks. TRAP: Believing the buttons only affect a single row or column, rather than rotating the entire long cycle.

ESTABLISHED: The red square at the top-right is a hard barrier. The gray block is collectible. The map follows a strict six-pixel grid. FAILED: Walking around the barrier. Moving the blue block into the red zone. Ignoring the red cap switch. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top area without interacting with the switch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move six pixels. SPACE respawns at the start.

GOAL: Rotate a plus-shaped block to match a target pattern within a strict action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; standing on a plus cell rotates it clockwise. RULE: Yellow energy depletes per move; collect ring power-ups to refill it before running out. TRAP: Assuming you can finish all rotations before refilling; you must visit rings early to sustain the long path.

GOAL: Guide two linked squares to touch and swap sides. CONTROLS: Arrows move both squares simultaneously, mirroring left and right. RULE: The squares must occupy adjacent cells, reversing their left-right order. TRAP: Assuming both squares always move; obstacles can block one, causing them to separate unexpectedly.

GOAL: Place an octagon inside the ring and two diamonds at the endpoints without overlapping shapes. CONTROLS: Click to move shapes; click gray diamonds to flip their orientation. RULE: Shapes must not overlap; the octagon fits perfectly within the ring’s center. TRAP: Assuming the ring is filled when the octagon enters; you must also place the diamonds at the specific endpoints to complete the level.

GOAL: Place two yellow blocks onto specific marker spots on the top row. CONTROLS: Click buttons to rotate the large serpentine track or the short top-row track. RULE: Rotating the top row rearranges blocks within the shared segment, changing their relative spacing. TRAP: Assuming only the main loop matters; you must use the top-row rotation to separate the blocks correctly.

GOAL: Align the plug's red feet with the socket's red contacts. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the plug three spaces at a time; Space rotated it ninety degrees. RULE: The feet only connect when they sit directly on top of the contact points. TRAP: Thinking the white shell had to fit inside the green slot caused unnecessary collision checks.

GOAL: Align the plug’s yellow head with the bar’s yellow gap to complete the connection. CONTROLS: Click the plug body to move it horizontally; click the bar’s yellow segment to shift its position. RULE: Only the yellow parts interact; black sections are inert obstacles that define the path. TRAP: Believing clicking the black bar segments or blue blocks does anything; they are static scenery.

GOAL: Reach the white target tile to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character two spaces in that direction. RULE: You jump over the middle square, landing on the second one regardless of what is there. TRAP: Thinking you must stop at walls or that the middle square blocks you wastes turns.

GOAL: Slide the L-shaped black piece until its white dots align perfectly with the gray divider lines. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece exactly three units in the pressed direction, matching its thickness. RULE: The piece only clicks into place when its internal white dots sit directly on the divider, turning them solid. TRAP: Assuming one press moves one unit; movement is three units, so miscounting steps causes overshooting the target.

GOAL: Reach the exit while avoiding the red enemy. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one space per press. RULE: The red enemy lunges only when you are in its line of sight. TRAP: Believing the enemy moves on a fixed timer wasted time waiting instead of breaking line of sight.

GOAL: Navigate the green block to the yellow core. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the green block; clicks rotated red and blue structures. RULE: The green block must remain on solid surfaces, avoiding voids and obstacles. TRAP: Rotating structures without checking for immediate collisions caused unnecessary resets.

GOAL: Align the piece and its reflection by moving them separately. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active item; Space switches focus between the piece and the mirror. RULE: The mirror reflects the piece across its vertical center line. TRAP: Moving both items blindly causes overlap; you must toggle focus to position each independently.

GOAL: Arrange three boxes into the four-slot zone to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move or rotate; Space picks up or drops a box. RULE: A box slides one cell when pushed, but lifts freely when held. TRAP: Thinking you must push boxes into place; carrying them is faster and avoids blocking.

GOAL: Slide the plug right to fill the gap. CONTROLS: Clicking the shared edge pushes both panels right; clicking the plug moves it independently. RULE: The plug is trapped by the shared panel's edge, so you must widen the shared area first. TRAP: Moving the plug alone fails because the shared panel blocks its path until expanded.

GOAL: Align five glyph rotators to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP rotates the selected glyph. RULE: Match each slot’s rotation to the corresponding blue target symbol. TRAP: Assuming all slots rotate simultaneously; they act independently, so verify each before moving on.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit while destroying three stationary red enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile in the chosen direction. RULE: Landing on a red from a side perpendicular to its facing direction destroys it instantly. TRAP: Assuming reds move or attack when you are not directly in front of them; they remain stationary unless approached head-on.

GOAL: Decode the hidden word sequence using glyph rotation and position. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate selected glyphs to match reference shapes. RULE: Identity is rotation-invariant; match shapes, not orientations. TRAP: Assuming visual order equals logical order; naming schemes shifted mid-solve.

ESTABLISHED: The cup sits at rotation plus forty-five with white ink and twenty-five purple cells. Only left and right rotations plus dash painting change the board; up and down do nothing. FAILED: Up and down inputs produced no movement. Dash attempts at zero rotation failed to hit the exact fifty-cell count target. GOAL IS NOT: A specific visual picture of the bottom half filled, nor a precise geometric alignment of the cup. CONTROLS: Left and right rotate the cup. Clicks switch ink color. Space applies the current ink to the cup's path.

GOAL: Translate yellow glyph words into their blue counterparts to fill seven empty slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between slots. Up cycles through available blue symbols for the current slot. RULE: Segment the bottom yellow bar into valid words, then place the matching blue word in the corresponding slot. TRAP: Assuming single glyphs are always words ignores that some blue words are longer, breaking the seven-slot limit.

GOAL: Place three shapes onto yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; space shifts the mirror line. RULE: Shapes reflect across the mirror; align the mirror so reflections hit targets. TRAP: Moving pieces down before aligning the mirror caused collisions and misalignments.

GOAL: Translate the yellow glyph sequence into blue slots by splitting it into known words. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles the slot’s letter. RULE: The total blue slot count must exactly match the sum of the matched words’ lengths. TRAP: Assuming each glyph maps to one letter; you must group glyphs into whole words first.

GOAL: Align three panel stems with colored gaps by adjusting panel heights. CONTROLS: Click buttons to grow or shrink adjacent panels, moving their stems up or down. RULE: Each panel must stay within board bounds and not overlap its neighbor’s limits. TRAP: Assuming buttons work independently; ignoring that shrinking one panel can block its neighbor’s movement.

GOAL: Move the plug to the exit using directional switches. CONTROLS: Click switch bars to toggle horizontal signals, stems for vertical, then click the plug to execute. RULE: A black bar with a white stem signals left; a black stem signals down. TRAP: Believing switch order is irrelevant; signals execute sequentially, so misaligned paths cause immediate failure.

ESTABLISHED: Solid rock bands at rows 30 and 36 permanently block access to the upper region. Three green blocks sit trapped between these bands. The bottom white bar is a step counter, not a drain. The player is confined to the lower basin. FAILED: Attempting to reach the upper region. Testing buoyancy. Assuming the bottom row was a drain hole. Clicking greens in the rock band to open passages. GOAL IS NOT: Draining water out of the bottom. Reaching the upper cave section. Breaking the solid rock bands at rows 30 and 36. CONTROLS: Clicking green blocks turns them into water. GOAL: Align two moving shapes with their static mirror-image targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space switches to the next object in the cycle. RULE: The mirror’s reflection point dictates the target position; shapes must overlap their reflected counterparts. TRAP: Assuming Space cycles randomly or skipping the mirror adjustment before moving pieces causes misalignment.

GOAL: Guide the plug to the target socket by dragging it along the visible path. CONTROLS: Click any dot on the trail to instantly move the plug to that specific location. RULE: The plug acts like a snake; moving forward consumes dots ahead and leaves a trail behind. TRAP: Assuming clicks move the plug a fixed distance. They actually teleport it directly to the clicked spot, regardless of range.

GOAL: Position the cup below the block to pour. CONTROLS: Arrows tumble the cup around the block; only moves that keep it touching the block work. RULE: The cup must remain adjacent to the block at all times. TRAP: Trying to move the cup to the bottom slot directly from the side is blocked by the ground.

GOAL: Rotate tiles until each displays its specific target glyph. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between tiles; UP rotates the current tile’s glyph. RULE: Match the required symbol for each position to complete the pair. TRAP: Assuming identical tiles need no change; check each slot against its unique target.

GOAL: Fill the empty slots in the center box with colored blocks to match the specific color sequence displayed at the top. CONTROLS: Click a colored block at the bottom to select it, then click an empty slot in the center to place it. RULE: The order of colors shown in the top row dictates exactly which color must go into each slot from left to right. TRAP: Assuming the bottom blocks are arranged in the correct order to be clicked sequentially, rather than matching the top reference pattern.

GOAL: Guide the falling block into the cup notch at the bottom. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the blue platform; Space drops the block. RULE: The block lands on the platform, which then carries it horizontally. TRAP: Arrows move the platform, not the block itself.

GOAL: Reach the exit while dodging a moving orange guard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step per turn. RULE: You could not share a cell with the guard at any moment. TRAP: Believing you could pass through the corridor while the guard was elsewhere, ignoring its oscillating patrol pattern.

GOAL: Guide two crosses to cover matching colored dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches to the other. RULE: A cross covers a dot when its line passes through the dot’s center. TRAP: Assuming dots vanish immediately; they only count when aligned with the cross’s arm.

GOAL: Reorder falling blocks to form the correct word sequence. CONTROLS: Click a block to lift it, then click a target slot to swap or place it. Press space to submit the solution. RULE: Clicking an occupied slot swaps the held block with the one already there. TRAP: Assuming occupied slots reject actions, forcing unnecessary moves to the tray instead of direct swaps.

GOAL: Place seven colored blocks into specific slots across three connected boxes to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click a tray block to select it, then click a target slot to place it. Press space to submit the solution. RULE: Match the block letter to the slot’s hidden requirement, ensuring pipes align correctly between the top, green, and blue boxes. TRAP: Assuming ring positions draw visible pipes wastes time; they only indicate which box a slot connects to, so ignore visual gaps.

GOAL: Guide the glowing wire tip into the blue socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys retract or extend the wire head; moving up or down shifts the entire assembly vertically. RULE: The wire tip must pass directly through the socket’s center, not just touch its edge. TRAP: Moving the wire blindly without first retracting the tip to clear obstructing sockets causes the path to block.

GOAL: Align three colored shapes to cover specific grid points. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; space cycles which shape is active. RULE: Every target dot must be covered by a line of its matching color. TRAP: Assuming one color alone could clear the level; all three required alignment.

GOAL: Align colored blocks into target slots to match a hidden sequence pattern. CONTROLS: Click a tray piece to pick it up, then click a grid slot to drop it. Press space to confirm the solution. RULE: A pre-placed block acts as a fixed anchor, locking the correct starting position for the entire color sequence. TRAP: Assuming any starting offset works for the color cycle, ignoring how the fixed block restricts the valid alignment.

GOAL: Position the X, diamond, and line to align with specific targets. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; spacebar switches selection. RULE: Shapes move in fixed steps; verify the whole shape shifts together, not just one arm. TRAP: Assuming the diamond is separate V-shapes; it is one rigid object, so moving one side moves all.

GOAL: Arrange two horizontal barriers to channel fluid into three separate collection notches simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the selected barrier; mouse clicks switch which barrier is active; Space pours the liquid. RULE: Barriers must align perfectly with notch openings to catch flow, while leaving gaps elsewhere to prevent overflow. TRAP: Assuming the first barrier’s position was correct; ignoring the second barrier’s misalignment caused premature spilling.

GOAL: Grow both colored bars until their end-dots land precisely on the center of the plus signs. CONTROLS: Click the green glyph to extend the horizontal bar; click the yellow glyph to extend the vertical bar. RULE: Bar lengths must equal 2 plus a multiple of 3, making only specific grid positions reachable. TRAP: Assuming any alignment with the plus shape wins; only the exact center dot placement counts.

ESTABLISHED: The 3x3 panel toggles cells. A specific four-cell diamond pattern triggers a surge. The marker slides vertically or swaps halves when full-height. FAILED: Single clicks, pairs, and random patterns do nothing. Clicking the diamond cells in isolation caused a surge without clearing the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply turning all cells green or creating the diamond pattern alone. CONTROLS: Clicking cells toggles their color. Up/Down moves the marker or swaps track halves.

GOAL: Direct rising fluid into three specific upper notches using movable barriers. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the selected bar; clicking selects a new bar; Space pours the fluid. RULE: Fluid rises vertically until blocked, then spreads horizontally along the underside of the barrier above. TRAP: Assuming fluid stops at the first barrier ignores that it slides sideways past the ends to find open notches.
GOAL: Merge two blocks to clear the bar. CONTROLS: Click near a block to shift it five rows. RULE: Blocks vanish when their edges touch. TRAP: Assuming merges happen at distance ten.

GOAL: Route the cable through the purple ring to secure the connection. CONTROLS: Clicking the empty socket swaps its position with the active plug. RULE: Center the bead by placing endpoints symmetrically opposite each other across the ring. TRAP: Assuming the bead moves independently; it is fixed at the cable's midpoint and only shifts when endpoints change.

ESTABLISHED: The arms are 2-wide wedges, not 1-wide corridors. Specific cells like (3,7) are solid walls despite being inside the wedge shape. FAILED: Assuming the entire black wedge area is walkable space; the ball gets stuck at specific internal boundaries. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the top row; the path requires navigating a specific snake-like route within the wedge. CONTROLS: Directional inputs move both balls simultaneously, but individual balls stop if their target cell is a wall.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the yellow block with the bracket. CONTROLS: Click green to rotate clockwise; click red to rotate counter-clockwise. RULE: Each arrow click shifts the entire ring by one position in its respective direction. TRAP: Clicking the bracketed block does nothing; you must use the arrows to move the ring itself.

GOAL: Guide the plus and X shapes to cover matching colored dots without overlapping wrong colors. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Spacebar switches control between shapes. RULE: Shapes only paint dots when their arms physically touch them, ignoring distant colors. TRAP: Assuming shapes stay painted after moving; you must reposition each shape to touch its specific target dots at the end.

GOAL: Place both balls on the top row simultaneously to finish the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the first ball normally, while the second ball mirrors horizontal moves. RULE: You control two objects at once; one input shifts both pieces in opposite horizontal directions. TRAP: Assuming arrows move only one ball independently causes wasted turns and unexpected collisions.

GOAL: Align the blue block with the panel center using only six moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker; clicks triggered the surge mechanism. RULE: The surge expands the marker only when the blue block sits in the center column. TRAP: Assuming the marker grows regardless of position wasted time on misaligned surges.

GOAL: Guide two yellow tokens to specific target slots using rotation switches. CONTROLS: Three buttons rotate different loops of tiles, shifting token positions along the paths. RULE: Tokens move only when the loop they occupy is rotated; shared tiles allow switching loops. TRAP: Assuming tokens stay in one loop; ignoring shared junctions prevents reaching distant targets.

GOAL: Match the outer ring of blocks to the center dial’s pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a block rotates the surrounding ring of blocks clockwise. RULE: The center dial shows the target configuration; align the outer ring to it. TRAP: Believing you must change the dial’s rotation instead of the outer blocks’ positions.

ESTABLISHED: Covering the cross triggers a white ring flash on both boxes. The logo rotates 90 degrees clockwise per cover, regardless of approach direction. Ring flashes are generic event effects, not unique state indicators. FAILED: Matching the target counter state via rotation alone did not clear the level. GOAL: Reduce all pegs to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click an adjacent empty spot to jump over a neighbor. RULE: Each move captures the jumped piece, removing it from the board permanently. TRAP: Believing any jump works; ignoring alignment causes failed moves and wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the yellow and orange blocks to their matching brackets. CONTROLS: Rotate the left or right loop to shift blocks along their circular paths. RULE: Blocks transfer between loops only when they occupy the two shared crossing cells. TRAP: Assuming blocks stay in their starting loop; ignoring the shared cells prevents the necessary swap.

GOAL: Match the grid to the patterns shown on the dials. CONTROLS: Click a block to change its color. RULE: White means active; gray means inactive. TRAP: Thinking gray blocks should be clicked to activate them.

GOAL: Match every grid cell to the color required by its adjacent dial constraints. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between red and orange. RULE: Each dial dictates the specific colors of all its neighboring cells. TRAP: Assuming a fixed starting color; some cells needed toggling twice to reach the correct state.

GOAL: You needed to seal the corridor with the block to win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block. RULE: The block had to fully cover the passage opening. TRAP: Thinking the cross was the target wasted time; it was just a distractor.

GOAL: Insert the plug's tips into the socket's nubs to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the plug right and down; spacebar checks status without moving. RULE: The plug stops immediately when its tips touch the red nubs, signaling connection. TRAP: Assuming you must overlap the nubs completely; pushing further triggers a collision block instead of a win.

GOAL: Transform the grid to match the target pattern within the action limit. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color from blue to red to orange, then back to blue. RULE: Each click advances the color by one step, so reaching a target color requires a specific number of presses. TRAP: Assuming the goal was to match the starting state or that colors were fixed, rather than needing to cycle through intermediate hues.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange blocks to their specific target squares using two independent sliding cycles. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shift all blocks horizontally along their rows. Up and down arrows shift all blocks vertically along their columns. RULE: All blocks move together on every click, so you must plan paths that align both colors simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming you can move blocks independently causes wasted clicks; remember that every action affects every block on the board.

ESTABLISHED: The level is split into top and bottom halves connected only by a left corridor. A red 5x5 pad blocks this corridor, making the level unsolvable via navigation alone. FAILED: Moving the blue block did not clear the path. The red pad remained static across all frames. GOAL IS NOT: Simply navigating around the red pad or using the blue block to bypass the barrier. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue block. Space toggles a HUD state but does not remove the red pad.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking a green piece moves the white dot to it; clicking walls, rings, or active pieces does nothing. The dot remains attached to the clicked piece. FAILED: Clicking empty corridor cells, ring interiors, or purple walls produced no visible change or movement. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing a plug in the left ring or moving the dot to a static wall cell. CONTROLS: Mouse clicks select pieces to transfer the dot; the dot follows the selected piece's position.

ESTABLISHED: The rotating arm pivots at the dark red block's corner. FAILED: Walking along the arm while it rotates. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the end of the horizontal arm. CONTROLS: Red glyph rotates arm to vertical; blue glyph moves block to top socket; arrow keys move token.

GOAL: Move the block to the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; clicks rotated arms and swapped blocks. RULE: Blocks can pass through dark red zones but not walls. TRAP: Rotating an arm while the block is on it causes failure.

GOAL: Slide charcoal onto yellow while black moves oppositely. CONTROLS: Left moves charcoal right; Down moves both down. RULE: One key press moves each block one space in opposite directions. TRAP: Assuming Right moves charcoal right; it actually pushes charcoal left.

GOAL: Break the wall to rise, then slide left to touch the pink cross and finish the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; clicking a block destroys it and lifts the player up. RULE: Destroying a block beneath you causes an automatic, continuous rise until you hit a ceiling. TRAP: Thinking the pink cross is an obstacle; it is actually the goal you must reach and touch.

GOAL: Paint the target block's lower rows purple using the cup's contents. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved or rotated the cup; space poured the contents. RULE: Gravity kept contents fixed relative to the cup, so rotating it 180 degrees let it sweep upward to paint. TRAP: Assuming contents poured downward regardless of rotation caused failed attempts to position the cup correctly below the target.

GOAL: Turn all block cells purple by satisfying hidden color requirements. CONTROLS: Clicking a plain block toggles only that cell; clicking a cross toggles itself plus its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Crosses affect a plus shape, not the full 3x3 area, so plan toggles to avoid ruining adjacent solved cells. TRAP: Assuming crosses toggle diagonals or the entire block causes wasted moves and unsolvable states.

GOAL: Slide the charcoal block onto the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; Space toggles movement modes. RULE: Space determines if you move the piece or the wall. TRAP: Do not assume pieces pass through walls; check clearance first.

GOAL: Move the white piece to connect with the purple and yellow assembly, then position the blue piece to snap into place. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece. Arrows move it one step. The spacebar rotates it ninety degrees clockwise. RULE: Pieces only lock when red tips align perfectly with matching sockets on other connected parts. TRAP: Rotating first may block movement paths; always check clearance before turning a piece near others.

GOAL: Slide the yellow plug left into the exit slot. CONTROLS: Click the top blue button to shift the plug right; click the bottom blue button to shift it left. RULE: Only the blue buttons trigger movement; clicking the plug, the bar, or empty space does nothing. TRAP: Trying to click the plug itself to move it wastes time and clicks.

GOAL: Navigate the player to the exit tile within the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Each movement consumes one action from the shrinking bottom bar. TRAP: Believing the bar length indicated health; it is strictly a step counter.

GOAL: Align the plug’s green tip with the marker by moving wall sections. CONTROLS: Clicking below the top bar raises the middle wall; clicking below the bottom bar lowers the base. RULE: Moving the middle wall up shifts the base down, keeping total wall height constant. TRAP: Thinking you must move the plug directly; the plug is fixed, and alignment comes from shifting the wall sections.

GOAL: Align five sliding barriers to let the block pass through the maze. CONTROLS: Four buttons shift specific barriers up or down to open paths. RULE: Barriers are linked; moving one forces its neighbor to move in the opposite direction. TRAP: Assuming buttons work independently wastes moves; always track how each click shifts adjacent barriers.

GOAL: Guide the plug through the filled slots to reach the empty target space. CONTROLS: Click a slot to command the plug to move toward that location. RULE: The plug can only jump to a slot if it is within three positions away. TRAP: Believing you can click any distant slot to teleport the plug directly to it.

GOAL: Match the bottom pink row to the top grid’s paired symbols. CONTROLS: Arrows move between slots; UP and DOWN cycle the shape in the current slot. RULE: Each top pair reveals which symbol belongs in the matching bottom slot. TRAP: Assuming rotation matters; only the symbol identity counts, not its orientation.

ESTABLISHED: Three sockets exist. One is currently empty. FAILED: Filling the pink bar did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Filling the pink bar. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug. Space attaches to a socket or drops it.

GOAL: Place three sockets into the bar's empty slots to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; Space attaches a socket when adjacent or drops it into a slot. RULE: Sockets must be attached to the plug's tip before moving them to their target positions. TRAP: Assuming placed sockets stay highlighted; they revert to charcoal once detached, misleading you into thinking placement failed.

GOAL: Clear the corridor by neutralizing the red block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; vertical moves avoid danger. RULE: The red block only attacks horizontally when you are in its row. TRAP: Moving vertically is safe, but entering the block’s cell directly causes death.

GOAL: Rotate seven labeled dials to match a target row using arrow keys. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves selection; Up/Down rotates the active dial one step. RULE: Dials cycle vertically; Up and Down move in opposite directions through the sequence. TRAP: Forgetting navigation costs extra actions, as pressing Up/Down repeatedly without moving stays on one dial.

GOAL: Split one falling block into two halves and guide them into separate collection bins without losing any pieces. CONTROLS: Press the arrow keys to shift the horizontal bar, and press space to drop the block. RULE: Each half slides outward on the bar until it hangs fully off the edge, then falls straight down. TRAP: Assuming the bar position doesn't matter, or that pieces stop sliding at the bar's edge rather than falling when unsupported.

GOAL: Trace the spark path to the socket by arranging five glyph segments to match the target shape. CONTROLS: Click bars to toggle horizontal segments, click stems to toggle vertical segments, and press the blue button to launch the spark. RULE: Each glyph combines a bar and stem to form a specific letter or symbol; only the correct sequence creates a continuous path. TRAP: Assuming the spark moves automatically after every click wastes time; you must manually launch it after each configuration change.

GOAL: Arrange the four colors in the slots to match the order shown in the top row. CONTROLS: Click a colored button to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: The sequence must follow the left-to-right order of the hint row at the top. TRAP: Assuming the bottom buttons are already in the correct order or ignoring the specific target sequence.

GOAL: Rotate the dial to match the hidden symbol pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys spin the dial forward or backward. RULE: Each click shifts the symbol to its neighbor in a fixed loop. TRAP: Assuming the dial resets to zero; it maintains its position between turns.

GOAL: Guide the shrinking snake head into the body to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head; clicking the body completes the pattern and shrinks the head. RULE: The head toggles between large and small sizes every time the body pattern is completed. TRAP: Believing the head stays large; you must shrink it by completing the pattern to fit through narrow channels.

GOAL: Decode a row of blue glyphs into yellow by passing them through a hidden two-step cipher using the provided key pairs. CONTROLS: Arrow keys navigate the cursor to select specific glyph slots for editing or verification. RULE: Each blue glyph must first transform into a pink intermediate, which then transforms into the final yellow result. TRAP: Assuming direct blue-to-yellow mapping ignores the necessary pink step, causing you to reject valid intermediate states.

GOAL: Shrink the large block tip to fit the narrow gate. CONTROLS: Click white cells to complete the pattern; arrow keys move the block. RULE: The passage is two units wide, so the block must be two units wide to pass. TRAP: Assuming the block moves one unit per arrow press; it actually moves by its full width.

GOAL: Align the ends of two sliding plugs with their matching target crosses. CONTROLS: Click the directional arrows on the side panels to extend or retract each plug. RULE: The level completes only when both plugs are simultaneously positioned exactly on their respective crosses. TRAP: Believing a single plug alignment triggers victory; passing over the cross without stopping there does not count.

GOAL: Arrange seven letter tiles to spell a hidden word in the correct color-coded slots. CONTROLS: Click a tile to select it, then click another slot to swap their positions. Press Space to check your answer against the secret word. RULE: Swapping requires two clicks: one to pick up a tile, one to drop it into a new spot. TRAP: Clicking a filled slot selects it rather than clearing it, wasting actions if you assume it removes the tile.

GOAL: Clear the path to the exit by destroying three hostile blocks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one space; entering a block's cell destroys it. RULE: Blocks only attack when you are directly in front of them at distance two. TRAP: Approaching a block from the side or back is safe, even if it faces your row.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored blocks into the correct sequence to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click two blocks to swap their positions; press space to submit the arrangement. RULE: The light beam indicates which panel contains the next correct block, guiding the left-to-right order. TRAP: Assuming the beam points to the block’s current location instead of its target panel causes wasted swaps.

GOAL: Place seven colors into a chain of linked panels to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click bottom tiles to select colors, click empty slots to place them, press space to confirm. RULE: Follow the physical connection order, filling each panel segment left-to-right before jumping to the linked neighbor. TRAP: Assuming all panels fill simultaneously or ignoring that connector slots force a detour to other panels.

GOAL: Move colored crosses to cover matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the active cross three spaces. Space switches between crosses. RULE: Crosses only collect dots aligned on their horizontal or vertical arms. TRAP: Assuming single-space moves wastes turns; remember every press jumps three units.

ESTABLISHED: Blocks N and b occupy specific columns. The rail mechanism sweeps rows 20-27. Moving UP shifts blocks six rows. Blocks outside swept rows remain stationary. FAILED: Moving N and b separately caused conflicts. Pushing N up while b was elsewhere, or vice versa, displaced the other block into incorrect bands due to overlapping sweep ranges. GOAL IS NOT: Placing blocks in bands 25-28 or 13-16. The final configuration requires both blocks in band 19-22 with specific column alignments. RULE: The bead always sits exactly halfway between the moving plug and the fixed gray anchor. TRAP: Believing the plug itself must reach the target; only the midpoint matters, so overshoot to compensate.

GOAL: Align the tip’s vertical split to pulse right into the pink socket. CONTROLS: Arrows roll the tip, flipping its split axis; clicks complete the pattern. RULE: A vertical split emits a horizontal pulse; a horizontal split emits a vertical one. TRAP: Assuming orientation is static; rolling the tip changes which direction it pulses.

GOAL: Align the ring so the target color lands on the top-left marker. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring clockwise; click the green arrow to rotate it counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click rotates the entire ring by one full side, moving blocks between corners and edges. TRAP: Believing you must click individual blocks to move them; only the side arrows affect the ring's position.

GOAL: Trace the hidden diamond outline by moving the red marker along its visible edges to reveal the shape. CONTROLS: Space selects the red marker; arrow keys move it one step along the diamond’s path. RULE: The marker must stay on the continuous slope of the diamond’s edge to keep the line intact. TRAP: Thinking the marker can jump across gaps; it cannot skip pixels, so stop if the line breaks.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over neighbors into empty holes. CONTROLS: Click a peg to see valid moves, then click a highlighted hole to jump. RULE: Jumps only happen horizontally or vertically, never diagonally. TRAP: Assuming you can jump anywhere; you must land exactly two spaces away with a peg directly between.

GOAL: Place three shapes to cover all eight dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches between them. RULE: Shapes move three cells per press; dots must align with arms or centers. TRAP: Assuming the line had a vertical arm; it only covers horizontally, forcing dots into specific rows.
GOAL: Rotate the block to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block. RULE: Entering the cross rotates the block. TRAP: Believing covering the cross wins; you must rotate it first.

GOAL: Move yellow pieces to marked crosses by rotating three horizontal tracks. CONTROLS: Top, middle, and bottom buttons shift their respective rows left or right. RULE: Each button click rotates its row by one position; the direction depends on the button color. TRAP: Assuming all buttons rotate in the same direction wastes moves; check each row's independent shift direction.

GOAL: Move the active block to cover the ring's interior space. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active block; clicking a block makes it active. RULE: Blocks overwrite ring pixels, destroying them upon contact. TRAP: Assuming ring walls block movement like solid barriers wastes time.

ESTABLISHED: Two blocks merge into a single 50-pixel object. The maze corridors form mirrored loop shapes. HUD bars decrease steadily with actions but show no sudden jumps or progress feedback. FAILED: Merging blocks, pressing SPACE immediately after merging, and moving blocks to apparent entry points or maze pockets did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing both original blocks on target cells, as merging does not prevent this condition. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move blocks. Merging combines two blocks into one. SPACE performs an action that currently yields no visible change or win.

GOAL: Move two distinct letters onto their matching colored cross targets. CONTROLS: Two button pairs rotate two separate loops; one pair spins the left loop, the other spins the right loop. RULE: Each button click rotates its entire loop by one position, shifting all letters along the path. TRAP: Assuming buttons move single letters; they actually cycle the whole ring, requiring you to align targets by rotating the entire chain.

GOAL: Match the grid’s block colors to the pattern shown on its side widget. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid block toggles its color between blue and red. RULE: Widget gray cells require blue blocks; widget white cells require red blocks. TRAP: Assuming the widget reflects the current state rather than the target pattern.

GOAL: Paint seven specific tiles red to match the hidden pattern revealed by the two compass widgets. CONTROLS: Clicking a tile toggles its color between blue and red; clicking widgets does nothing. RULE: White arrows on a widget point to tiles that must be red; green arrows point to blue. TRAP: Assuming the widgets update after clicking or that the center orange color dictates the target hue.

GOAL: Move the yellow and orange blocks to the bottom-right target squares. CONTROLS: Left and Right shift blocks along horizontal rows; Up and Down shift blocks along vertical columns. RULE: Rows and columns form single continuous loops; moving past the edge wraps the block to the opposite side of the entire row or column. TRAP: Assuming rows and columns are separate independent tracks; they are actually one long cycle each, so wrapping jumps between the top and bottom halves.

GOAL: Recolor all ring cells to match their widget centers. CONTROLS: Click ring cells to toggle their color. RULE: White rings match the center's color; gray rings take the opposite. TRAP: Assuming all rings need the center's color ignores the gray cells requiring the other hue.

ESTABLISHED: The plug cannot leave the top band on the right side because white cells block downward and rightward movement. FAILED: Attempting to push the plug down or right to force the snake to advance or turn up the vertical strip. GOAL IS NOT: Navigating the plug down the vertical line or into the wider white areas to the right. CONTROLS: Moving the plug left or up is possible; moving down or right fails due to white cell collisions.

GOAL: Align the plug’s tips with the socket’s opening to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the plug; rotation was fixed in this instance. RULE: The plug must sit directly adjacent to the socket, touching but not overlapping. TRAP: Assuming the plug needed to fully insert into the socket caused unnecessary movement attempts.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug with the blue socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Clicking empty space moves the plug; clicking the plug itself wastes a turn. RULE: The plug only moves toward the direction indicated by the charcoal arrow. TRAP: Believing you could drag the plug or click it directly to place it.

GOAL: Seat four blocks into their target zones using only straight-line moves. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the active block until it hits a wall or another block; clicks select a new block to move. RULE: Blocks stop immediately upon collision, so you must push them against walls or other blocks to position them correctly. TRAP: Assuming a block can stop mid-grid; without an obstacle, it will slide all the way to the edge, overshooting the target.

GOAL: Guide the gray piece to overlap the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece one step per press. RULE: Match the piece's head and tail exactly to the yellow outline's shape and position. TRAP: Believing the black reflection was a solid obstacle requiring complex navigation, rather than ignoring it as a visual effect.

GOAL: Paint the canvas to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the brush. Click swatches to select colors. Space applies paint. RULE: The brush paints the color currently selected in the palette. TRAP: Clicking a swatch fails if the action is formatted incorrectly, leaving the default white brush active.

GOAL: Recolor the grid so each widget’s center matches white and neighbors match gray. CONTROLS: Click widgets to cycle through color assignments for the surrounding ring. RULE: The HUD legend lists only the colors present in the target solution. TRAP: Assuming all widgets share a single global partner color; each widget has its own specific partner.

ESTABLISHED: Red and blue pieces toggle between two distinct positions when clicked. Red rotates around a dark red center; blue shifts location entirely. FAILED: Clicking different parts of the pieces (crown vs brim) did not change the toggle behavior; they still just swapped between the two known states. GOAL IS NOT: A pipe-connecting puzzle requiring the red piece to occupy two places simultaneously, as it cannot split. CONTROLS: Clicking the red piece rotates it around its pivot. Clicking the blue piece moves it between its two fixed slots.

GOAL: Align the plug head with the green marker on the moving bar. CONTROLS: Clicks on the top bar adjust the middle white gap width, which directly limits the plug's maximum travel distance. RULE: The plug's range equals the width of the middle white region; widening this gap extends reach. TRAP: Believing the plug range was fixed; adjusting the gap width, not just moving the plug, was key.

GOAL: Paint the canvas by stamping specific geometric shapes onto the grid. CONTROLS: Arrows move your stamp position. Clicks select paint colors. Space applies the selected shape. RULE: Each stamp position paints a unique pattern, like triangles or rows, based on its location. TRAP: Assuming stamps cover identical areas wastes moves; verify each position’s unique footprint before painting.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the exit using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys trigger fixed two-cell jumps in that direction. RULE: Jumps require a clear landing spot; blocked paths halt movement. TRAP: Assuming continuous sliding until a wall causes wasted actions.

ESTABLISHED: The maze is a grid of walls, rooms, and green blocks. Removing a green block opens its 5x5 area. Adjacent wall rows may or may not open depending on whether they separate open rooms or other wall bands. FAILED: Removing the green block at rows 37-41 did not open row 36, leaving the shaft capped. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing one block to create a direct path; complex wall interactions exist. CONTROLS: Clicking a green block removes it. The game tracks budget per level.

GOAL: Align the gray shape's bounding box with the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; clicks switch selection between the block and the line. RULE: The line's center must land on a specific column, requiring the block to shift one step left first. TRAP: Thinking the block could stay fixed; its position restricts valid line centers to multiples of three.

GOAL: Paint the grid using two colors. CONTROLS: Move cursor, select color, click brush to stamp. RULE: The large stamp covers all cells where row plus column is less than ten. TRAP: Believing the small brush works anywhere; it only paints when the cursor is at the starting pose.

GOAL: Move liquid to set three specific levels while keeping the rest empty. CONTROLS: Buttons transfer liquid between adjacent columns in fixed amounts. RULE: A transfer fails completely if the receiving column would exceed its wall height. TRAP: Thinking you can dump into the fullest column first; it must drain before accepting more.

GOAL: Reach the exit without triggering the red trap. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one step in the chosen direction. RULE: The red tile kills only when approached from the left; entering from below is safe. TRAP: Believing the red tile is lethal from any direction wasted time testing other angles.

ESTABLISHED: Absorbed boxes turn the player white and widen them; released boxes turn gray. The frame is twelve units wide, matching two boxes plus the player. FAILED: Placing boxes normally into the frame did not win. Moving boxes without absorbing them had no effect. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing boxes into the frame slots. CONTROLS: Space absorbs adjacent boxes, turning the player white and growing wider.

GOAL: Move the plug up the diagonal line to reach the blue socket at the top. CONTROLS: Click a dot to slide the plug to that spot, pushing intervening dots backward. RULE: The plug can only move up to three slots per click. TRAP: Clicking too far away does nothing; you must plan short hops to reach the top.

GOAL: Move two blocks to form a mirror pattern across a horizontal line. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the mirror line or the selected block; clicks select a block. RULE: Blocks must align perfectly with their faint reflections on the opposite side of the line. TRAP: Assuming the line moves with the block; you must position the line first, then move the block to match.

GOAL: Move the lifted box down one row and left three columns, then release it into the target frame. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player and attached box together. Space dropped the held box at the player's location. RULE: Carrying a box forces it to move exactly with the player until released. TRAP: Assuming the box stays fixed while moving the player; you must walk the box into position before dropping it.

GOAL: Arrange four colored blocks in the middle box to match the target order shown at the top. CONTROLS: Click a block at the bottom to select it, then click a gray slot in the center to place it. RULE: The top row displays the exact sequence of colors required from left to right. TRAP: Assuming you can drag blocks directly is wrong; you must use a two-step click to select and then place.

GOAL: Match five rotating symbols to their static partners by cycling through seven possible shapes. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the selector between slots. Up and down arrows rotate the current symbol forward or backward in the cycle. RULE: Each slot cycles through the same seven shapes, but starts at a different position, so you must rotate until the shape matches the partner. TRAP: Assuming the cycle order is identical for every slot wastes time; always rotate and check the shape after each press rather than calculating blind.

GOAL: Fill both cups at once. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bar; Space pours goo. RULE: Position the bar so goo drips into both cup openings simultaneously. TRAP: Thinking you must fill cups separately or adjusting height, when only horizontal alignment matters.

GOAL: Reach the exit while eliminating three saw traps without triggering their lethal zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character one square in the chosen direction. RULE: You safely remove a saw only by entering its square from a direction opposite to its facing side. TRAP: Moving directly into a saw’s target square causes instant failure, regardless of the saw’s presence.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket by setting the correct switch pattern. CONTROLS: Toggles adjusted switch states; clicking the bulb energized the circuit to test alignment. RULE: The number of active switches determined the travel distance, matching the gap size. TRAP: Assuming partial activation worked; only a fully synchronized pattern allowed the plug to move.

GOAL: Align seven rotating slots to display the target alphabet sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows switch active slots or rotate the current slot’s glyph forward and backward. RULE: Each slot follows a fixed cycle order, so shortest path is the smaller difference between current and target positions. TRAP: Assuming all slots share the same rotation direction wastes actions when one slot runs opposite.

GOAL: Align two crosses so their arms cover all scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide crosses three units; Space confirms or switches focus. RULE: Each cross arm must pass through specific dot clusters simultaneously to clear the level. TRAP: Believing obstacles block movement during the slide; they only matter at the final resting position.

GOAL: Move the pulse to the right edge to transmit the signal. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the pulse along the wire. RULE: Transmission only occurs when the pulse touches the far right limit. TRAP: Waiting for a new pattern to appear; the grid stays clear after the first success.

GOAL: Extend the green plug tip to meet the red cross target. CONTROLS: Clicking the right glyph extends the plug length by three units. RULE: The plug tip must align exactly with the center of the cross. TRAP: Assuming the dot marks the tip; it actually trails behind the plug's end.

GOAL: Light the three grid cells to shrink the pulse, then guide it through the narrow gap into the top socket. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to transmit energy; press arrows to move the pulse. RULE: Transmission shrinks the pulse width, allowing it to pass through obstacles too wide before. TRAP: Trying to force the large pulse through the connector fails; you must shrink it first.

GOAL: Translate a hidden word into a specific seven-symbol sky sequence using a provided legend. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the selected glyph slot through its cycle; selector arrows move the cursor between slots. RULE: The word’s pattern uniquely dictates how to segment it into legend phrases, fixing the target sequence length. TRAP: Assuming the cycle order is static; you must probe the first slot to map the true rotation direction before solving.

GOAL: Position three floating bars so rising goo flows through gaps to reach a target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the selected bar; clicking selects a different bar; space confirms the layout. RULE: Goo rises only through empty vertical channels, requiring precise horizontal alignment to avoid blocking the flow. TRAP: Assuming bars could overlap to save space; overlapping bars block the goo entirely, forcing a single-file channel design.

GOAL: Collect orange dots inside boxes by aligning shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape. Space switches control to the next shape. RULE: Shapes pass through boxes; dots vanish only when a shape’s pixels cover them. TRAP: Mistaking shape arms for dots led to false positives; rely on pixel count drops, not just visual overlap.

GOAL: Guide the player to the saw target while dodging a bouncing orange enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step on even-numbered cells. RULE: The orange jumps two cells vertically, reversing direction at grid edges. TRAP: Moving straight to the target causes a collision; waste moves to sync timing.

GOAL: Grow a small shape into a large yellow block and guide it into the waiting blob. CONTROLS: Click near a square to drop a new one, merging if close enough, or click a block to shift it. RULE: New drops merge instantly if within a small gap, but moving a block requires clicking adjacent to it. TRAP: Assuming merging finishes the level; you must still push the combined block into the target zone.

GOAL: Rotate seven yellow glyphs to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted the selected glyph; Up cycled through the shape sequence. RULE: Each slot’s shape followed a fixed seven-step cycle, requiring minimal presses to align. TRAP: Assuming shapes could be swapped between slots wasted time; each slot only cycled its own specific set.

GOAL: Guide the energy pulse to the blue socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the pulse one grid step in that direction. RULE: Transmission clears obstacles, opening new paths through previously blocked areas. TRAP: Assuming obstacles are permanent wastes time; they vanish after a transmission, so move immediately into the cleared space.

GOAL: Guide goo through three cups by aligning risers with openings. CONTROLS: Arrows move bars; clicks select them; space releases goo. RULE: Bars must sit directly above cup gaps so goo flows vertically. TRAP: Thinking horizontal overhangs block flow; they only matter if they cover the gap.

GOAL: Sequence colored tiles through a split path to match target slots. CONTROLS: Click a tile to pick it up, then click an empty spot to drop it. RULE: The sequence flows continuously, snaking from the top row through the connector into the bottom row, then back up. TRAP: Assuming the top row finishes entirely before entering the bottom row; the path interleaves them, requiring you to treat the grid as one continuous loop rather than separate lines.

GOAL: Place seven letters into slots to spell the target word. CONTROLS: Click a tray letter, then click a slot to place it; press space to confirm. RULE: Read the main row left to right, inserting the sub-box letters wherever their colored connector appears. TRAP: Assuming slots fill sequentially across all boxes ignores the nested insertion order at connector points.

ESTABLISHED: The ring moves freely upward from center 32 without dragging the green block. FAILED: Moving the ring to center 20 to impale the red block remains unconfirmed and risky. GOAL IS NOT: Simply raising the ring without ensuring the red block remains reachable. CONTROLS: UP moves the ring and extended arm upward; LEFT retracts the arm and pulls impaled blocks left.

GOAL: Place two shapes into marked slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space switches focus. RULE: Only one shape moves at a time; toggle to switch targets. TRAP: Moving all pieces at once fails; you must alternate between them.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so the yellow block aligns with the fixed bracket. CONTROLS: Clicking the red cross rotated the ring counterclockwise one step per click. RULE: The yellow bracket marked the exact destination for the unique yellow block. TRAP: Assuming the green plug or red cross needed physical movement wasted clicks on irrelevant interactions.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg by clearing the others. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it and reveal valid landing spots, then click a highlighted spot to jump. RULE: A jump is only legal if an adjacent peg sits directly between the start and an empty landing cell. TRAP: Assuming you can jump over empty space or move to an occupied cell; every hop must capture exactly one neighbor.

GOAL: The block had to physically enter the top monitor box to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block one step in the chosen direction. RULE: Only reaching the designated target zone triggers a win; visual changes were secondary. TRAP: Believing the changing legend icon was the goal wasted time analyzing symbols instead of navigating.

GOAL: Guide both blocks to the center line to form a single merged shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: The puzzle ends immediately when the two blocks touch at the center. TRAP: Pressing SPACE to confirm the layout is unnecessary and wastes a turn.

ESTABLISHED: The plug sits at the ring, but the level remains active. FAILED: Moving the plug to the ring did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the plug on the ring is insufficient. CONTROLS: Dragging the plug moves it along the wire path.

GOAL: Align shapes to match swatch colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move shapes; Space switches active shape. RULE: Shapes must cover swatches of their own color, not the legend's pairing. TRAP: Trusting the legend caused a long detour; ignoring it for direct color matching saved time.

GOAL: Color the final panel's blocks to match the hidden pattern shown by the small glyph inside it. CONTROLS: Click individual blocks in the panel to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: Gray marks in the glyph mean the block stays blue; white marks mean it must turn red. TRAP: Assuming the glyph was just decoration; it was actually the direct solution key for the empty panel.

GOAL: Guide two blocks to collide safely without entering hazardous zones. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Blocks stop if blocked by walls or hazards, preventing unintended collisions. TRAP: Assuming hazards act like walls causes failed moves; treat them as lethal barriers.

GOAL: Guide the head to its matching ring while positioning the pulse correctly. CONTROLS: Arrows move the head; pushing the pulse sends it sliding until it hits a wall. RULE: The head cannot pass through purple walls, but the pulse can slide through them temporarily. TRAP: Believing the head could follow the pulse’s trail through the wall wasted time; the wall remains solid for the head.

GOAL: Use glyph clues to turn specific blocks orange. CONTROLS: Click blocks to flip their color state. RULE: White marks in a glyph mean that surrounding block must be orange. TRAP: Assuming gray marks require action or that blocks start in a neutral state.

GOAL: Place yellow tokens into two specific bracketed spots to finish the level. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to rotate the main loop and slide the top or bottom rows left or right. RULE: Each move shifts a whole line, so a token’s final spot depends entirely on where it starts relative to the target. GOAL: Click the correct blocks to turn them orange so they match the hidden pattern behind the glyphs. CONTROLS: Clicking a block toggles its color between red and orange to reveal or hide it. RULE: Each glyph reveals the shape of blocks that must be orange in its surrounding area. TRAP: Assuming glyphs only show red blocks; they actually define the orange target shape, not the remaining red ones.

GOAL: Swap yellow and orange tokens into their matching colored brackets. CONTROLS: Green plugs rotated the left or right ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Tokens only change rings when passing through the two shared central cells. TRAP: Assuming you could move tokens directly between rings without rotating through the shared intersection.

GOAL: Rotate the plug and move it to merge red tips with red nubs to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug three cells; Space rotates it ninety degrees clockwise. RULE: Red components only merge when they perfectly overlap, signaling the win. TRAP: Assuming rotation keeps the plug stationary costs time, as the center point shifts.

GOAL: Guide the green token to the yellow box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicking plugs rotates colored bars. RULE: Rotate bars only when the token is outside their path to avoid penalties. TRAP: Believing you can rotate a bar while the token is inside it, which causes a failure.

GOAL: Recolor the grid to match the hidden pattern defined by the glyph symbols. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color through the available palette options. RULE: Each glyph acts as a local legend where the center color applies to white subcells and the other present color applies to gray ones. TRAP: Assuming glyphs are independent ignores how overlapping regions force consistency, leading to contradictory color assignments.

GOAL: Slide the mirror-image blocks until the shadow block covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move both blocks symmetrically; LEFT/RIGHT spreads or closes the gap, UP/DOWN shifts vertically. RULE: The blocks are perfect reflections across the center line, so every move affects both equally. TRAP: Treating the blocks as independent or ignoring that arrows move them three cells at a time.

ESTABLISHED: Blue box starts and recalls to the dock. SPACE recalls the box to the dock, leaving a ghost marker at the previous location. Arrow keys move the active blue box. FAILED: Pressing SPACE after moving the box off the dock did not create a controllable gray clone. The gray HUD icon does not represent a deployable unit. GOAL IS NOT: Filling white pits with boxes or moving a secondary gray box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue box. SPACE recalls the blue box to the dock, leaving a ghost at the departure point.

GOAL: Slide the shadow onto the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece; Space switches selection between the black shape and the line. RULE: Moving the black shape moves the shadow in a mirrored vertical path, but only selecting the line allows horizontal shifts. TRAP: Believing arrows move the shadow directly; you must first move the black shape down, then switch to the line to nudge the shadow left.

GOAL: Fill specific grid cells with pink while keeping others dark, respecting button effects. CONTROLS: Click grid cells to toggle color; click buttons to toggle their base and adjacent neighbors. RULE: Pressing a button toggles its own state and the four surrounding cells simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming buttons only affect neighbors; ignoring the button’s own toggle led to extra correction clicks.

GOAL: Rotate the tip to face left, then fire a pink pulse down the arm to destroy the barrier. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate and move the tip; clicking lights the pulse path. GOAL: Paint a specific multi-color pattern on the grid using stamping tools. CONTROLS: Click swatches to choose colors, click brushes to select tools, and press Space to stamp the active brush onto the canvas. RULE: Brushes automatically change color to match the last selected swatch, allowing you to move between poses without re-selecting colors. TRAP: Clicking a white swatch erases the brush color, causing the Space key to do nothing visible on a white canvas.

GOAL: You needed to move three endpoints to form a triangle. CONTROLS: Clicking an endpoint selected it; clicking a target moved the selection. RULE: Only one endpoint could be active at a time, forcing sequential moves. TRAP: I wrongly thought I could chain multiple endpoint moves without deselecting.

GOAL: Place black pieces on yellow targets using mirrored shadows. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected piece; SPACE cycles selection between line, L, and T. RULE: Shadows reflect across the horizontal line; moving the line adjusts all shadow positions. TRAP: Believing pieces move independently; you must position the line first to align reflections.

ESTABLISHED: The reference panel depicts the full ten-row stack as solid purple. Current state has mixed purple and white blocks in the lower stack rows. The cup currently holds a purple block. GOAL: Fill the grid with four colored regions defined by diagonal boundaries. CONTROLS: Click colors to select, Space to stamp, arrows to move.
